To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) a goal-based round-trip method for system development can support the strategic analysis and the construction and evaluation alternatives for the system-to-be; 2) the strategic i* models can be used as a basis for the generation and evaluation alternatives; 3) the generation of alternatives can be done systematically, and 4) the reuse of strategic i* knowledge can be supported.

we propose a method to develop information system that supports the strategic analysis of business process and the systematic construction of alternative models, based on goal-oriented models and the round-trip engineering approach, which is supported by the use of requirements engineering techniques.
we have developed a method that supports the round-trip engineering of strategic i* goal models for information system development and that we have evaluated the method by means of a case study.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a method for the construction of strategic i*-based information systems.
the development of a goal-based round-trip engineering method, which supports the construction of strategic i∗ models and the generation and evaluation of strategic alternatives.

the use of i* models to support the strategic and prescriptive analysis of the business process, and the use of goal-oriented requirements engineering techniques to support the generation and evaluation of strategic alternatives.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the proposed method allows to: (a) identify the strategic goals of the current business process, (b) generate and evaluate alternatives to achieve those goals, and (c) select the best alternative to be implemented.

the proposed method is a goal-oriented round-trip engineering method that supports a systematic generation and evaluation of system alternatives, based on the analysis of strategic models of the existing process.
the proposed method is able to support the strategic design of information systems in a systematic way.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we propose a method that supports the strategic analysis of a business process, the generation of alternatives, and the evaluation of those alternatives, using a goal-based model as the core artifact of the method.
we have developed a method for the construction of goal-based alternatives, which is supported by a tool, called Goal-Builder.
the method proposed here is a systematic and goal-based way to support the development of strategic information systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a goal-based approach is useful not only to support the strategic view of the system, but also to guide the development process.
goal-oriented modeling can be used as a formalism to support strategic information system development, which is a promising approach to improve the success of information system development projects.

strategic models, as a result of the analysis of the current business process, can be reused to support the specification of the new process and the generation of alternatives, which are the starting point for the design and implementation of the new system.
